text:
ash: anyone on Windows seeing redwoodctl localserve return 401 right after installer login? I used the MSI from releases, login said success but the sample app can't find the token.

lee: what does `redwoodctl config get profiles.path` show and where did the MSI actually write files?

ash: config shows C:\Users\ash\AppData\Roaming\redwoodctl\profiles but the MSI created C:\Users\ash\AppData\Local\Redwood\profiles\default\token.json

maya: yup, APPDATA vs LOCALAPPDATA mismatch. The CLI looks in %APPDATA% by default. Short-term fix: set the REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR env var to the path the installer used or create a junction: `mklink /J "%APPDATA%\redwoodctl\profiles" "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Redwood\profiles"`.

ash: setting REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR fixed it for me, localserve picks up the token now.

lee: filing issue PKG-1292 "Windows MSI writes profiles to LocalAppData instead of %APPDATA%" and a small installer patch. QA should test fresh install and upgrade flows, and machine-wide vs per-user installs.

maya: another headless edge: `redwoodctl auth login --headless` tried to spawn the OS opener in our Windows CI container and failed with "could not open browser". For headless/CI we should only print the URL and skip any spawn.

lee: noted; adding PKG-1293 "headless login must not attempt to open browser in non-GUI CI/container environments". Suggested detection: if not isatty or DISPLAY/XDG_SESSION_TYPE missing, don't spawn.

maya: also saw token schema drift: some old token.json use `expires_at` while new code expects `expiry`. CLI should accept both for at least two releases and provide a migrate command.

ops-bot: canary deploy scheduled: installer/msi-profiles-fix -> windows-canary at 2026-04-01T02:00Z

ash: will validate canary on Monday and report results here. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
